To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evolution of the ATP related compounds and volatile compounds in desalted cod was affected by thermal treatment, and that the two blanchings (water and steam blanching) were more effective than the microwave heating in the conservation of desalted cod.

the two blanch treatments (water blanched and steamed blanched cod) are more effective than the microwave treatment (control and microwaved cod), in the preservation of the volatile fraction and ATP related compounds during the 28 day storage period.
the two blanch treatments were more effective on the preservation of desalated cod than microwave heating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the volatiles and ATP related compounds of desalted cod during storage at 4 ° C.
the evolution of volatile fraction and ATP related compounds during the storage of desalted cod thermically treated.
the evolution of volatile fraction and ATP related compounds in desalted cod, thermally treated (steam blanching, microwave heating and water blanching), and stored at 4°C.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two blanchings treatments were more effective on the preservation of desalinated cod, than the microwave treatment.
microwave heating is not a suitable method to preserve the initial quality of desalted cod, as the other two thermal pre-treatments (blanching).
the blanching treatments (water and steam) were the most effective in preserving the initial odor of the desalted cod.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the blanching treatments, and especially steam blanching, were more effective than the microwave heating in the prevention of the development of the volatile fraction and the spoilage of desalted cod during storage.

the blanching treatments, water blanching and steam blanching, were more effective than the microwave heating in the reduction of the initial K1-value, which was the parameter that better correlated with the sensory quality of the desalted cod.
water and steam blanching were the most effective treatments for the preservation of desolated cod, and microwave heating was less effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the volatile fraction and ATP related compounds as quality indexes in desalted cod is useful to evaluate the effectiveness of the thermal pre-treatment in its preservation.
the volatile fraction and the ATP related compounds can be used to assess the freshness of desalted cod during storage.
the use of the K1-value as an index of spoilage is more appropriate than the use of the ATP related compounds.
